summary.en: Build abstract syntax trees, share proven common subexpressions with value numbers, and invalidate sharing when values change.
summary.bn: তুমি ট্রিতে এক্সপ্রেশনের গঠন দেখবে, আর একই হিসাব নিরাপদে একবার করতে DAG বানাবে।

notes: Python programs use the standard library and were executed with Python 3.12.14.

practice.title: Compare tree structures
practice.statementHtml: Draw an AST and DAG for (a+b)*(a+b), and explain the difference in parent relationships.
hints: One DAG node may have two incoming uses.
practice.answerHtml:
For (a + b) * (a + b), a concrete parse tree includes E, T, F and punctuation nodes. The AST needs only multiplication, two additions, and their operand leaves. Parentheses disappear because the tree shape preserves their grouping.

Structural comparison
RepresentationNodes retainedParent ruleMain use
Concrete parse treeGrammar symbols and punctuationOne parent per non-root nodeExplain a derivation
ASTOperations and meaningful operandsOne parent per non-root nodeSemantic processing and translation
Expression DAGOperations and shared valuesA node may have several parentsExpose repeated computations
AST:                    DAG:
       *                       *
     /   \                   /   \
    +     +                 v     v
   / \   / \                 (+)
  a   b a   b                / \
                            a   b

An AST occurrence represents a particular use of an operator in source. In the DAG, the multiplication node has two edges to the same addition node. The graph has no directed cycle because a value cannot depend on itself through an unfinished arithmetic computation.

practice.title: Assign value numbers
practice.statementHtml: Number every occurrence in (a+b)*(a+b) and give the resulting shared TAC.
practice.answerHtml:
A value number is an internal identity for a value known to be equivalent to another occurrence. Keep a map from leaf values or operator-and-operand keys to numbers. When a key already exists, reuse its number. Otherwise create a node and assign a new number.

Complete value numbering for (a+b)*(a+b)
VisitLookup keyNumber returnedNew node?
First aleaf(a0)v1Yes
First bleaf(b0)v2Yes
Left addition(+, v1, v2)v3Yes
Second aleaf(a0)v1No
Second bleaf(b0)v2No
Right addition(+, v1, v2)v3No
Multiplication(*, v3, v3)v4Yes

The suffix 0 identifies the incoming version of each name. The resulting TAC needs t1 = a + b and t2 = t1 * t1. Generate nodes in dependency order so an operation appears after its operand nodes. Sharing the graph is not enough if your code emitter still recomputes a node for each incoming edge.

practice.title: Handle a reassignment
practice.statementHtml: Value-number x=a+b; a=a+1; y=a+b without reusing an invalid sum.
hints: The current value of a changes after its assignment.
practice.answerHtml:
Consider x = a + b; a = a + 1; y = a + b. The final addition is not the first addition. The new a value needs a fresh value number, while b can keep its incoming identity. Keep a current-name map and update the destination after computing each right-hand side.

Value numbers across a reassignment
Statement or leafKeyNew identityCurrent name mapping
Incoming a, b, 1leaf(a0), leaf(b0), constant(1)v1, v2, v3a:v1, b:v2
x = a + b(+, v1, v2)v4x:v4
a = a + 1(+, v1, v3)v5a:v5, x:v4
y = a + b(+, v5, v2)v6y:v6

The old value v1 remains a valid graph input for x even after a stops naming it. This is why value numbering separates a variable's current spelling from the value already captured by an earlier computation. An implementation that mutates leaf a in place would incorrectly change x's meaning.

practice.title: Evaluate sharing safety
practice.statementHtml: Decide whether repeated scalar sums, loads, calls and volatile reads can be shared.
hints: Look for changes to the values or visible effects.
practice.answerHtml:
Scalar names are the easy case. Now imagine p and q can point to the same location. A store through q may change the next load through p. Even if the text *p appears twice, sharing those loads needs alias information or a conservative invalidation rule.

When repeated text does not prove a shared value
SequenceTempting reuseWhy more evidence is needed
x = a+b; y = a+bReuse scalar sumSafe if neither operand changes
x = a+b; a = 1; y = a+bReuse first suma now names a new value
x = *p; *q = 7; y = *pReuse first loadp and q may alias
x = f(); y = f()Reuse first callf may change state or return another value
x = volatile_input; y = volatile_inputReuse first readReads can be separately observable

A classroom DAG can clear memory-expression entries after an unknown store or call. That loses some optimisation opportunities but preserves correctness. Better alias analysis can prove that particular locations are independent. Never turn an absence of information into a claim that two memory accesses are unrelated.

quiz.prompt: How many addition nodes remain in the DAG for (a+b)*(a+b) with unchanged inputs?
quiz.explanation: Both additions have the same operator and operand value numbers.

quiz.prompt: What does an AST omit from the concrete parse tree?
quiz.explanation: Punctuation and pass-through grammar nodes can disappear while structure preserves meaning.

quiz.prompt: Why is a+b after assigning a a different value-number key?
options: The operand identity for a changed
quiz.explanation: Keys describe operand values rather than only their source spellings.

quiz.prompt: Which expression order must a subtraction key preserve?
What extra mechanism lets a DAG emitter avoid duplicate instructions?
options: A visited set or topological schedule
quiz.explanation: Shared nodes must be emitted once rather than once per incoming edge.

quiz.prompt: Why may a store through q invalidate a cached load through p?
quiz.explanation: Both pointers could address the same location without a proof to the contrary.

quiz.prompt: What can increase after common-expression sharing?
quiz.explanation: Retaining a value for several uses can increase register pressure.

quiz.prompt: Which key can safely reuse the pure integer sum v1+v2 under the stated rule?
quiz.explanation: The operator and both operand identities must agree unless an additional proven equivalence applies.

options: Integers and reals have identical semantics
quiz.explanation: Changing grouping can change rounded intermediate results.

quiz.prompt: What does the current-name map track?
options: The value number presently denoted by each name
quiz.explanation: Assignments update this map while earlier value nodes remain available to their existing users.

keyPoints.en: An AST retains grouping while removing grammar scaffolding.
keyPoints.bn: গ্রামারের বাড়তি নোড বাদ দিলেও AST-তে হিসাবের গঠন থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A DAG can give several uses the same value node.
keyPoints.bn: DAG-তে একই মানের নোড একাধিক জায়গা থেকে ব্যবহার করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Value-number keys include the operator and operand values.
keyPoints.bn: Value number খুঁজতে অপারেটর আর অপার্যান্ডের মানের পরিচয় মিলাও।

keyPoints.en: Assignment changes the current value identity of a name.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যাসাইনমেন্টের পরে নামটি নতুন মানকে বোঝাতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Unknown memory effects can invalidate expression sharing.
keyPoints.bn: মেমরিতে কী বদলেছে জানা না থাকলে আগের হিসাব আবার ব্যবহার কোরো না।
